title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Détermination du groupe des relations rationnelles sur Q'. The neighbouring transcribed pages (Azumaya algebras, separability of Hom_A(M,M)) are an unrelated typescript; this page stands alone in the cycles/motives folder.

Setup. Let T be an algebraic torus over Q. Over C, T_C = D_C(M) is diagonalisable with character lattice M. The absolute Galois group pi_1 = pi_1(Q, C) acts on M through a finite quotient pi acting faithfully, the splitting group of T. Z(M) = Z[M] is the ring of virtual characters of T_C, and pi acts on it.

Grothendieck ring. K(T) = Z(M)^pi is the ring of Galois-invariant virtual characters. This is the Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional Q-representations of T: irreducible Q-representations correspond to pi-orbits in M, and their characters are the orbit sums. It is a finitely generated Z-algebra.

Geometric reformulation (the N.B.). Z(M) is the affine ring of the split torus S = D_Z(M) over Z, on which pi acts by group automorphisms. K(T) is the affine ring of the quotient scheme D_Z(M)/pi.

Problem: describe the 'effective' elements of K(T), meaning classes of actual representations (orbit sums with non-negative coefficients). This is the positive cone / semiring structure on K(T), the 'structure d'effectivité'.

First guess (marked '??'): effective characters are those taking values >= 0 on S(R)^0 = (R_{>0})^r. Necessity is clear, since each monomial lambda_1^{u_1}...lambda_r^{u_r} is positive there. Sufficiency is false: 1 - t + t^2 is positive on R_{>0} without being a non-negative combination of monomials. Hence the doubt, and the question of how to define a 'metric' effectivity structure.

Second attempt: the 'standard procedure'. Fix a cocharacter i_1: G_{m,C} -> T_C, equivalently i_1^*: M -> Z, as in the usual filtrations. This gives Z(M) -> Z(Z) = Z[t, t^{-1}], hence alpha: G_{m,Z} -> S, compatible with pi when the cocharacter is suitably invariant. For x in K(T) = Z(S)^pi, the effectivity condition relative to alpha is that x∘alpha, an element of the affine ring Z[t, t^{-1}] of G_{m,Z}, is a polynomial function. Equivalently, it stays bounded on G_{m,Z}(R) = R^* as t -> 0, i.e. all weights of x are >= 0. This is the familiar way effectivity (non-negative weights / Hodge types) is detected through a weight cocharacter.

The final lines are badly legible. They consider characters with non-negative multiplicities, a finite quotient of G_m, and replacing Q by R. They conclude that if dim T >= 3 the corresponding relation (presumably 'effective <=> positivity/boundedness criterion') is false.

Purpose: a test case for the structure of the Grothendieck ring of a tannakian category of motives, together with its effective cone, when the motivic Galois group is a torus (e.g. CM motives). Plausibly also a test of whether effectivity can be read off numerically/metrically.
errors: The criterion 'effective iff >= 0 on S(R)^0' is false as stated (e.g. 1 - t + t^2 on R_{>0}); Grothendieck himself flags it with '??'.
The map alpha: G_{m,Z} -> S commutes with pi only if the chosen cocharacter is pi-invariant (or one averages over its pi-orbit); the note '(qui commute aux pi....)' glosses over this.

Boundedness of x∘alpha as t -> 0 for one cocharacter only says the weights along that cocharacter are >= 0. It does not characterise non-negativity of the coefficients of x, consistent with the final 'Fausse'.

ideas.what: Grothendieck ring of Q-representations of a Q-torus equals Galois-invariants of the group ring of the character lattice, i.e. the affine ring of D_Z(M)/pi.
ideas.modern_name: Representation ring of a non-split torus; R(T) = Z[X^*(T)]^Gamma
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Ono, Voskresenskii for tori; Serre/Atiyah for representation rings)
ideas.where_published: Diagonalisable groups and D_Z(M) appear in SGA 3; the K-ring statement is not known to me there.

ideas.what: Seeking a 'structure d'effectivité' (positive cone) on the K-ring of a tannakian category, and testing whether effectivity is detected by positivity on real points S(R)^0.
ideas.modern_name: Effective cone / positive semiring in K_0 of a tensor category; positivity vs non-negative coefficients (Pólya-type questions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Effectivity structures on tannakian categories discussed around Saavedra Rivano (1972) and Deligne; Pólya (1928) for the positivity/coefficient problem

ideas.what: Detecting effectivity via a weight cocharacter G_m -> T: x is effective-relative-to-alpha if x∘alpha is a polynomial (weights >= 0), i.e. bounded as t -> 0 on R^*.
ideas.modern_name: Weight grading / effectivity via non-negative weights (effective motives, Hodge cocharacter)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck / Deligne / Saavedra (weight gradings in tannakian categories of motives)

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for a 'metric' characterisation of the effective cone in K(T) = Z[M]^pi for a torus T (motivic Galois group of CM-type motives). He tests positivity on S(R)^0 and boundedness along a cocharacter, and records that the corresponding criterion fails for dim T >= 3. A precise statement of which 'relation' fails, and what the correct characterisation is, is not worked out.
missed.quote: Les caractères effectifs sont ceux qui prennent des valeurs >= 0 sur les points de S(R)^0 ?? Comment définir une structure d'effectivité métrique ? ... si T est de dim >= 3, la relation ... correspondante est Fausse.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links effectivity of motives to real-positivity/Positivstellensatz phenomena (Pólya's theorem: positivity on the orthant implies effectivity after multiplying by a power of a fixed effective class). That gives a possible 'stable' version of his criterion. The connection does not seem to be made explicitly in the motives literature, but the page is too fragmentary to claim a result.

deep.surprise_reason: Exploratory, partly illegible scratch work on effectivity in the representation ring of a torus. The ideas (representation ring of a torus, effectivity via weight cocharacters) are standard. The only faintly interesting point is the explicit question of a 'metric' effectivity structure, its link to real positivity, and the claimed failure in dimension >= 3, which is left unresolved.
transcription_corrections: 'S = [-Z-] D_Z(M)' should read 'S = D_Z(M)' (the Z is crossed out).
'Le produit standard et de [-...-] fixer' likely reads 'Le procédé standard est de se fixer'.
'les variétés habituelles' is uncertain; possibly 'les filtrations habituelles'.
'λ_1^{u_1} λ_2^{u_2} ... λ_r^{u_r}' is a marginal monomial, not part of the sentence.

The condition line likely reads: 'La condition est, pour un x ∈ K(T) ≃ Z(S)^π, que x∘α ∈ Z[t,t^{-1}] = anneau affine de G_{mZ} soit une fonction polynomiale, i.e. restant finie sur G_{mZ}(R) = R^* pour t -> 0'.
Last line: 'la relation de [?] correspondante est Fausse'; the missing word is possibly 'positivité' or 'effectivité' (uncertain).
